sections.summary: P01-R1: walkIgnoredDirectory's nested-repository check no longer carries the `depth > 0` condition, so an ignored directory that is itself a checkout is emitted as `<dir>/` and never walked into — matching what `git ls-files --others --ignored` printed. The code edit was already on disk from the previous (rate-limited) Track R run; this run verified it, the comment explaining the depth-0 case, and the tests. The equivalence fixture now creates a top-level ignored `vendor/` with its own `.git` plus `vendor/lib/x.js`, and the legacy-vs-new comparison plus a dedicated case assert `vendor/` is listed and `vendor/lib/x.js` is not.

sections.summary: Probe fixes, all verified against the installed Wave 1 build (three live runs, app quit afterwards). (a) startup-probe: `paintsWithContentfulPaint()` re-reads the paint timeline for up to 1 s after the poll loop, so `fcpMs` is a number again (946/486 from the open call) and a new `fcpRendererMs` reports the renderer-clock figure the plan targets (308/164, was null in every Wave 1 sample). (b) open-folder-probe is one poll loop on a single 20 s deadline; ground truth from the live DOM showed two separate bugs: the explorer heading never contains the folder name (it holds the sidebar toggle and the branch), and `.project-tree` is a custom element that renders its rows into a shadow root, so every row query answered 0 — a shared `TREE_ROW_COUNT` now reads the shadow root (the startup probe's `rows` went 8 -> 44 from the same fix). `liveSnapshotMs` takes the earlier of a publish carrying a branch/`stage: 'live'` and the branch rendered for the active folder, reporting which won as `liveSource`; result: imux 16 ms, core-3 196 ms, better-code-diff 103 ms, all non-null, all `dom` (the P04 race wins and publishes nothing, which is exactly why Wave 1 saw nulls). (c) pr-open-probe's four serial waits are one loop on one 20 s deadline recording first-seen times plus `progressKinds` (first time and count of every kind, keyed on payload not on a kind list so `replace`/`checks` cannot be mistaken for a file page) and a `timedOut` flag: warm firstCodeViewMs 1,440 ms and cold 2,696 ms, against 106,205 ms before. (d) every probe prints a final `PERF {…}` line with median/min/max per headline metric.

reviewNotes:
DECISIONS / RISKY SPOTS, in the order I would review them.

1. R3 test hook. I added `mergeIgnoredPathsForTests(paths, 'current' | 'superseded')` to RepositoryService and widened `#mergeIgnoredPaths(ignoredPaths, run: AbortController | null)`. Reason: aborting a run kills its git child, so a superseded listing that still resolves is a window of a few microseconds between promise hops — not reachable from a test with two real git walks. The file already exposes `getContentSearchMetricsForTests`, `resetContentSearchMetricsForTests` and `getHeadCacheStatsForTests`, so the convention exists; if you would rather not ship the hook, the guard is one line and the `withIgnoredListingDeadline` run-identity test still covers the plumbing.

2. R6(b) deviation you should sanity-check: `window.repository` is frozen and non-configurable, so HOOKS cannot wrap the IPC methods. I verified this live (assignment is a silent no-op; `Object.defineProperty(window, 'repository', …)` throws). The substitute live marker is the branch rendered in `#repository-explorer .chrome-branch-button span` while the active world tab's label equals the folder. Two caveats: a repository genuinely in detached HEAD would never show a branch (a live git snapshot sets `branch` to the short head or 'No commits', so this only bites a hand-made snapshot), and a `kind: 'folder'` root has no branch button at all — for such a root only the publish path (`stage: 'live'`, which needs a rebuild to reach the app) marks it live. All four default FOLDERS are git repositories.

3. Re-opening the already-active folder in the open-folder probe reports ~0 ms, because its world already holds a live snapshot. That is arguably correct (re-opening a cached folder is instant), but it means the default FOLDERS list, which opens imux twice, produces one deliberately trivial sample.

4. The pr-open probe now burns its full 20 s per record when `done` never arrives — which is the current behaviour for a cached PR (only a `metadata` event reaches the renderer; finding PR-2 that Track D's P23 fixes). `timedOut: true` and `progressKinds` make that visible instead of inflating a metric. Three PRs therefore cost about a minute of deadline; `PR_TIMEOUT_MS` overrides it.

5. `statistics()` rounds to whole milliseconds in the PERF line only; the per-sample JSON keeps full precision (main-process marks are sub-millisecond). `median()` is unchanged, and with an even sample count it still returns the upper middle value.

6. Could not verify: the R5 ratchet (1,700,000) against a fresh build — Track C runs the build. If P14-P23 add anything to the pre-mount graph, that gate is the one most likely to trip first.

7. Shared-file discipline: repository.ts, repository.test.ts and contracts.ts were edited only with exact-string Edits inside my regions (refresh, refreshAfterExternalChange, #startIgnoredListing, #mergeIgnoredPaths + its hook, #refreshSnapshot, #refreshFolder and their tests; contracts.ts is one field plus its doc line). No needs-owner items came up — nothing outside my ownership needed changing.

8. Diagnostic scripts I wrote to get DOM ground truth live in the scratchpad (scratchpad/probe-dev/inspect-dom.mjs, inspect-tree.mjs, inspect-shadow.mjs), not in the repo. Live probe output is in scratchpad/results/r6-verify.jsonl.
